text:
.NET 11 Release Candidate 2 is available with a go-live support license for production use. It remains a prerelease version.

Changes worth reviewing:

• MSBuild: Project evaluation was 10-13% faster, with 16-34% lower allocations, in Microsoft’s tested Windows workloads.
• NuGet: Configure a minimum package publication age from the CLI to delay eligibility for automatic version selection.
• Blazor: QuickGrid’s AnchorMode and ItemComparer parameters no longer require experimental-warning suppression.
• Networking: Control initial HTTP/2 stream concurrency before the server sends its settings.
• Validation: A new DataAnnotations formatting API lets attributes supply arguments for localized messages.

If you are testing earlier previews, include the RC1-to-RC2 changes in your compatibility review.

text:
Air Fryer Garlic Dough Balls 👇

👉 For the dough:

400g strong white flour
7g sachet easy blend yeast
2 tsp salt
2 tbps olive oil
250ml tepid water

👉 For the garlic butter:

3 cloves garlic
7 g flat leaf parsley
50 g butter

1. Prepare the dough either by hand, in a food processor (the method I use), or in a bread maker. Mix all the ingredients together until a dough forms.

2. Remove dough and place in an oiled bowl and cover with cling film. Leave in a warm place for 30 minutes to 1 hour or until the dough has doubled in size.

3. Seperate the dough into golf ball sized pieces, you should get about 20 out of this recipe. 

Place them on a silicone liner in the air fryer, or you could use baking paper instead. 

Cook for 15 minutes in an air fryer at 180°C/350°C. Check on them at around 8 minutes and give them a gentle shake so that they can brown all over, also check to see how quickly they are cooking. (When I cook them in a Ninja Dual Air Fryer they cook much quicker than my Cosori air fryer.) 

The dough balls are ready when they begin to turn a golden brown colour.

4. Preparing The Garlic Butter
Melt the butter in a bowl or jug in the microwave, or in a saucepan on the hob. 

Using some kitchen scissors, or a sharp knife, chop the fresh parsley up and stir it into the melted butter. 

Use a garlic crusher and crush the cloves directly into the butter. Stir everything around before pouring it over the freshly cooked dough balls.

Pour the garlic butter over the dough balls as soon as they are out of the air fryer. Serve hot.

text:
Air Fryer Chicken Tikka Kebabs 👇

4 chicken breasts
150ml natural yoghurt
4 tbsp tikka curry paste
 
1. Dice the chicken into similar bite-sized pieces.
2. Add the yoghurt to a bowl and stir in the tikka curry powder or paste.
3. Submerge the chicken into the yoghurt and leave for at least 30 minutes.
4. Thread the chicken onto the kebab skewers and place them in the air fryer.
5. Cook at 180°C for 20 to 25 minutes. Check the chicken is cooked all the way through before serving.

text:
Slow Cooker Cajun Chicken 👇

8 boneless chicken thighs
400g chopped tomatoes
1 onion
1 sweet pepper
3 tbsp of Cajun seasoning
salt and pepper to season
 
1. Add everything to the slow cooker. There is no need to add any water or extra liquid.
2. Gently stir everything together.
3. Place the lid on top and set off on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 4 hours.
4. At the end of the slow cooker cooking time check the chicken is cooked all the way through. You can optionally shred the chicken and stir it through the sauce, or serve the chicken thighs whole. Suggested sides include rice or potato wedges.
